[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
Hugh was born about 1745. He was the son of [[Glasgow-1503|Hugh Glasgow]].  He passed away about 1756. 
== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-1499]] is assessed at 99% (proved). The published Larne monument places Hugh among Hugh Glasgow and wife Ann’s eleven children, with death on 30 November 1756 aged eleven. The 1745 chronology agrees separately.

Memorial-defined son Hugh→adult Hugh-1499.

Next useful test: Compare PRONI MIC/1B/6 against the monument.

Source basis already held: [https://archive.org/stream/ulsterjournalofa06ulstiala/ulsterjournalofa06ulstiala_djvu.txt Armorial Sculptured Stones of the County Antrim, Ulster Journal of Archaeology, Glasgow stone at Larne (https://archive.org/stream/ulsterjournalofa06ulstiala/ulsterjournalofa06ulstiala_djvu.txt), pp. 47–48.]; [https://web.archive.org/web/20101124184247id_/http://lifesweaving.com/Glasgow/Kilwaughter/Timeline.html Larne/Kilwaughter congregation register chronology]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.


=== Current research ===

The Larne memorial records Hugh, one of eleven children of Hugh Glasgow and wife Ann, as dying '''30 November 1756 aged 11'''. His calculated birth range is 1 December 1744 through 30 November 1745. This is consistent with the derivative register chronology's 1745 child, subject to checking <code>MIC/1B/6</code>.

This assessment draws on the cited records and public source material.<ref name="ProjectSource1">[https://archive.org/stream/ulsterjournalofa06ulstiala/ulsterjournalofa06ulstiala_djvu.txt Bigger and Hughes, Larne Parish Churchyard inscriptions].</ref><ref name="ProjectSource2">[https://web.archive.org/web/20101124184247id_/http://lifesweaving.com/Glasgow/Kilwaughter/Timeline.html Archived Larne/Kilwaughter chronology].</ref><ref name="ProjectSource3">[https://archive.org/details/ulsterjournalofa06ulstiala/page/47/mode/1up *Ulster Journal of Archaeology*, 2nd series, vol. 6, p. 47].</ref>
